topics.label: Lecture Introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture topic, acknowledging the complexity and importance of the complement system.

topics.label: Fundamentals and Architecture of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the core principles, nomenclature conventions, and the central pivotal role of C3 in the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of Complement Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three distinct recognition mechanisms that converge to trigger complement activation on pathogen surfaces.

topics.label: Complement Effector Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how activated complement components mediate pathogen destruction and stimulate the immune response.

topics.label: Host Regulation of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how regulatory proteins prevent inappropriate complement activation and damage on host cell surfaces.

topics.label: Clinical Consequences of Complement Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic covers the distinct disease presentations and vulnerabilities associated with deficiencies in specific complement components.

topics.label: Bacterial Evasion of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes how pathogens such as Staphylococcus aureus circumvent complement-mediated immune destruction.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the session on complement and previews the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
